$comment: Single source of truth for scope (Lesson 8). Every feature carries the triple: behavior + verification + state, plus evidence. Only the checker/verification script flips status to passing/done (Lesson 9). attempts/maxAttempts is a timebox: the maker increments attempts on every iteration it works a feature and MUST set status=blocked (with a reason in checkerNotes) once attempts reaches maxAttempts, instead of continuing to retry indefinitely. `context` is the handoff INTO implementation: the 1-3 files the feature touches, plus one line the implementer would otherwise rediscover. `evidence` is a LIST OF RUNS, not a paragraph: [{date, run: red|green, cmd, result}]. `behavior` and `falsifier` are ONE SENTENCE each. Each feature also carries kind (build|prove) and falsifier: the specific wrong implementation its verification would fail on, citing an `[INV-AREA-N]` id from docs/design/runtime-model.md or docs/design/tool-surface.md wherever one exists (docs/reference/invariant-contract.md). Cut 2026-08-20 from the approved design (loop/design-approval.json digest c0a83df4b8d6c5b2): 10 named components, build order per docs/design/tool-surface.md#Build-order (file-sync-watcher + readiness-gate before any capability tool; code actions last), enforced here as real dependency edges, not just prose.

features.name: Baseline green
features.behavior: Project installs Node dependencies, provisions a pinned JDT LS distribution fixture for the test suite, and runs the baseline gate to green from a clean checkout

context.note: package.json does not exist yet (greenfield) — this feature creates it, with check/typecheck/lint/build/test/test:integration scripts, since init.mjs's VERIFICATION block auto-runs whichever of those scripts exist. The JDT LS fixture step must honor A-005 (download+pin, JDTLS_HOME override for offline use) — reuse the download logic spikes/*.mjs already assume via a CLI-supplied jdtls-dir argument, don't re-derive it.

features.falsifier: a gate that exits 0 without actually installing deps or fetching the JDT LS test fixture — or one that runs a failing step and swallows it, which the bash version did — the baseline must be able to go red on either failure

2 tests passed: pinned archive installs and an absent fixture source fails explicitly
6 tests passed: harness/init.mjs executed install, fixture, and baseline-test steps; injected exit codes 23, 24, and 25 each made the gate red

features.checkerNotes: APPROVE: replayed the six-case integration suite and ./harness/init.sh successfully. The isolated startup-gate oracle observes install, fixture and baseline-test execution, and injected exits 23/24/25 independently prove failures propagate and stop later steps.

features.name: jdtls-provisioner: resolve/fetch/pin JDT LS + verify JVM
features.behavior: resolveInstall() locates a cached JDT LS distribution or downloads and pins one on first run, and refuses to proceed when no Java 21+ runtime is resolvable

context.note: A-005: download+pin on first run, never bundle; JDTLS_HOME env override must skip the network fetch entirely for offline use. Distribution is 51MB compressed/64MB extracted (docs/design/evidence.md) — the fixture download belongs to feat-001, this feature only resolves/verifies it.

features.falsifier: spawns JDT LS without checking the JVM version first, so a Java 17 machine gets an opaque JDT LS crash instead of a named-version error [INV-PROV-1]; or resolves whatever happens to already be in the cache instead of the pinned version [INV-PROV-2]; or, with JDTLS_HOME set, issues a network request or falls back to the cache/download instead of using that directory exclusively and failing closed with an error naming the path when it holds no resolvable launcher jar [INV-PROV-3]; or, with no valid cached install and the network unreachable, hangs past the deadline or surfaces an opaque stack trace instead of settling with an explicit error naming the pinned version, the unreachable host, and the JDTLS_HOME escape hatch [INV-PROV-4]

evidence.result: 6 assertion failures: JVM 20/17 were accepted, JDTLS_HOME was ignored, and invalid/unreachable installs did not reject
12 tests passed across JVM boundary, pin/cache handling, JDTLS_HOME fail-closed behavior, and bounded network failure
12 tests passed before implementation; no successful empty-cache download/install assertion exists to make red

features.name: lsp-client: Content-Length framing + id correlation
features.behavior: The LSP client frames every request with Content-Length headers, correlates responses to their pending request by id, and rejects every pending request the moment its underlying JDT LS process exits

context.note: Two different framings meet at this seam and confusing them is the design's own named most-likely-early-bug: LSP here is Content-Length-headers, MCP (owned by mcp-shim, not this component) is newline-delimited. Nothing else in the system should parse either framing directly.

features.falsifier: an id-correlation table that does not reject its pending entries when the underlying process exits, so a request in flight when JDT LS dies hangs forever instead of settling as an error [INV-POOL-3]

features.name: workspace-pool: per-workspace JDT LS lifecycle
features.behavior: The pool spawns exactly one JDT LS process per workspace identity with its own absolute -data directory, never spawning a second for a concurrent duplicate first call

context.note: -data is where the index lives; sharing one across workspaces corrupts both (docs/design/evidence.md). Derive the -data path from a hash of the realpath'd project root (X-005) so two paths to one project — including via a symlink — are one workspace, not two.

features.falsifier: two concurrent first calls for the same project each spawn their own JDT LS process instead of converging on one [INV-POOL-5]; or two live workspaces are given the same -data directory [INV-POOL-1]

features.name: Prove: the pool never exceeds its cap and never loses a warm -data dir
features.behavior: A burst of calls across more projects than --max-workspaces always evicts the least-recently-used idle workspace before spawning over the cap, and eviction never deletes the evicted workspace's -data directory

context.note: A-001 confirmed default cap is 3, evict LRU-idle after 15 min — use a small cap fixture value (e.g. 2) so the burst-over-cap scenario is fast and deterministic instead of waiting on the 15-minute idle window.

features.falsifier: a burst of calls beyond the cap spawns a process over the configured limit instead of evicting an idle workspace first [INV-POOL-2]; or an evicted workspace's -data directory is deleted instead of kept for warm restart [INV-POOL-4]
features.evidence: RED 2026-08-20: `npm run test:integration -- test/integration/pool-lifecycle.integration.spec.ts` — 0 passed, 3 failed. TCON-POOL-0001/0002/0003 each failed with an ERR_ASSERTION from the executable oracle: workspace-pool behavior required by INV-POOL-2/4 is absent because src/workspace/workspace-pool.ts does not exist. This is the expected pre-implementation red; Node loaded and ran the test file without a compile or fixture error.

features.name: Prove: a dead JDT LS process never leaves a call hanging
features.behavior: Killing a workspace's JDT LS process mid-request settles every in-flight request routed to it as an error within its deadline, never a hang and never a partial answer

context.note: This is the joint seam between lsp-client (owns the pending-request table) and workspace-pool (owns the kill/spawn decision) — kill the real child process, don't just close the stream, so the test exercises the actual exit-detection path.

features.falsifier: a request in flight when the child process dies hangs past its deadline instead of settling as an error, or resolves with a partial/stale answer [INV-POOL-3]
features.checkerNotes: BLOCKED (orchestrator, 2026-08-20): test-implementer dispatched ~19 times, same diagnosis every time — this oracle needs a real child process with an in-flight LSP request, a per-call deadline, and kill-signal handling, none of which exist yet (feat-lsp-client and feat-workspace-pool are both not-started). Unlike the 3 prove-features already oracled (provisioner/routing/pool-lifecycle), this behavior cannot be stubbed without fabricating the production interface. test-implementer has no attempts counter, so nothing else would have unstuck router rule 12 (oracle-before-implementation with no dependency-readiness check — reported as a harness defect, not worked around at the router level). Reroute here once feat-lsp-client and feat-workspace-pool are both done.

features.name: file-sync-watcher: on-disk changes reach JDT LS
features.behavior: The watcher translates every on-disk change under a workspace's source roots and pom.xml into the matching LSP notification

context.note: JDT LS does not watch the filesystem itself (spike C, docs/design/evidence.md) — an on-disk edit with no notification leaves JDT LS answering from a stale, well-formed-looking model with zero errors. This is why the design calls the watcher v1-blocking, not polish, and orders it before every capability tool.

features.falsifier: a rename or delete under a watched source root produces no notification, or produces the wrong change-type notification [INV-SYNC-2]; or a pom.xml edit only emits a source-file notification instead of triggering a project-configuration refresh [INV-SYNC-3]

features.name: readiness-gate: semantic-probe readiness
features.behavior: awaitReady(workspaceId, deadline) opens only once a semantic probe (resolving a known symbol from the workspace's own sources) answers non-empty, never on ServiceReady or ProjectStatus alone

context.note: ProjectStatus:OK and ServiceReady fire 13ms apart and BEFORE the final workspace-refresh progress notes (docs/design/evidence.md) — both are lies about readiness on their own; the probe result is the only thing this gate may trust.

features.falsifier: opens the gate as soon as ServiceReady or ProjectStatus:OK fires, without ever running the semantic probe [INV-READY-2]

features.name: Prove: no tool call ever answers from a stale on-disk view
features.behavior: Editing a workspace's source directly on disk and then immediately probing it through the readiness gate's semantic probe always yields either the post-edit answer or an explicit resyncing error, never the pre-edit one

context.note: Reproduce spike C exactly (docs/design/evidence.md `2_afterSilentDiskEdit`): delete a method's call site on disk, probe before the watcher's notification lands, and again after — the pre-notification probe state is the one INV-SYNC-1 forbids becoming a successful answer.

features.falsifier: a probe issued immediately after a silent on-disk edit resolves the deleted symbol and reports zero errors instead of either the corrected answer or an explicit resyncing error — the spike-C `2_afterSilentDiskEdit` state is reachable [INV-SYNC-1]
features.checkerNotes:
BLOCKED: the INV-SYNC-1 oracle has no specified callable seam until feat-file-sync-watcher and feat-readiness-gate exist.

TCON-SYNC-0001 through TCON-SYNC-0003 require a real watcher, its change-generation/quiescence contract, a real JDT LS subprocess, and readiness-gate semantic probes before and after notification. The design currently specifies only observable seams (`settledAt` and `awaitReady(workspaceId, deadline)`), not the watcher construction, generation handoff, probe result, or orchestration interfaces needed to write a behaviorally red test. Both owning dependencies are not-started. A test now could fail only on missing modules or invented interfaces, which is not valid red evidence. Reroute after feat-file-sync-watcher and feat-readiness-gate define and implement those seams.

features.name: Prove: readiness never lies and never hangs forever
features.behavior: A call during warm-up always gets isError plus progress rather than an empty successful result, and every waiting call is released or failed within its deadline even when a workspace never becomes ready

context.note: Simulate a workspace that never finishes warming (block the semantic probe forever) to prove the deadline path, not just the happy path — X-001's default deadline is still an open cross-cutting decision, so parameterize the test's deadline rather than hard-coding 30s.

features.falsifier: a call during warm-up returns [] instead of isError+progress [INV-READY-1]; or a call against a workspace that never becomes ready waits past its deadline instead of settling with an error [INV-READY-3]
features.checkerNotes:
BLOCKED: behavioral readiness oracle requires the not-started feat-readiness-gate callable interface.

The design only specifies awaitReady(workspaceId, deadline). It does not define how an integration test injects a permanently blocked semantic probe, observes per-call progress, or distinguishes the structured isError result from success. Writing the test now would invent feat-readiness-gate production signatures or produce only a missing-module/compile red, neither of which is valid red-first evidence. Implement and specify feat-readiness-gate first, then route this proof feature back to test-implementer.

features.name: daemon-supervisor: socket listener + single-instance lock
features.behavior: The daemon listens on $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/jdt-mcp.sock under a single-instance lock so concurrent launches converge on one daemon process, and shutdown always terminates every JDT LS child it spawned

context.note: Scope this feature to the Unix-socket path only (A-004: macOS/Linux for v1, Windows named-pipe deferred). The flagged Streamable HTTP front door (A-003) is out of scope for this cut — see DECISIONS.md, its Origin/localhost/auth invariants (X-010) are still undecided.

features.falsifier: N parallel jdt-mcp launches each start their own daemon instead of converging on one [INV-SHIM-2]; or daemon shutdown leaves a JDT LS child process running [INV-SHIM-4]

features.name: mcp-shim: stdio front end, connect-or-spawn
features.behavior: The shim connects to the daemon socket, auto-spawning the daemon under the lock when absent, copies newline-delimited MCP frames both ways, and never writes anything but a single valid MCP message to stdout

context.note: MCP stdio MUST NOT see embedded newlines and MUST see nothing on stdout but valid MCP messages (docs/design/evidence.md, spec quote) — every daemon log line, including errors during auto-spawn, goes to stderr or a file, never stdout.

features.falsifier: a daemon-side error or log line reaches stdout during a session, breaking the one-MCP-message-per-line contract [INV-SHIM-1]; or a daemon restart mid-session requires the client to re-initialize instead of the shim reconnecting transparently [INV-SHIM-3]

features.name: Prove: the daemon is a singleton and a restart is invisible to the client
features.behavior: N parallel shim launches always converge on exactly one daemon process, a stdout capture across a session containing daemon errors parses entirely as single-line MCP messages, and killing the daemon mid-session leaves the next call succeeding with no client-side re-initialization

context.note: Assert on the process table after shutdown (no orphaned JDT LS JVM) as well as on stdout content and pid count — INV-SHIM-4 is a process-table assertion, not a return-value one.

features.falsifier: two of N parallel launches each get their own daemon pid [INV-SHIM-2]; or stdout during a session with daemon errors contains a line that fails to parse as one MCP message [INV-SHIM-1]; or the process table after shutdown still holds a JDT LS child [INV-SHIM-4]
features.checkerNotes:
BLOCKED: daemon lifecycle oracle requires callable interfaces owned by the not-started feat-daemon-supervisor and feat-mcp-shim dependencies.

The design exposes only observable outcomes: jdt-mcp daemon status JSON, socket existence, shim stdin/stdout bytes, and process-table state. It does not specify the executable/CLI entry point, lifecycle commands, daemon-pid response, test fixture for spawning multiple live workspaces, or shutdown contract needed to exercise TCON-SHIM-0001 through TCON-SHIM-0003. Writing the integration test now would invent production interfaces or fail only because modules/commands are missing, which is not behavioral red evidence. Implement and specify feat-daemon-supervisor and feat-mcp-shim first, then route this proof feature back to test-implementer.

features.name: mcp-tool-layer core: registration, validation, positions, errors
features.behavior: The tool layer validates line/column arguments against the file's current content before any LSP call, converts every LSP position to the documented 1-based coordinate system at exactly this one boundary, and reports every failure as a structured error naming which case it is

context.note: Pure function of an injected LspFacade per the design (docs/design/architecture.md component table) — test against a fake facade here, the real pool/router/readiness/sync wiring is proved end-to-end by feat-prove-cross-process-integration. X-007 confirms 1-based; X-003's closed taxonomy is unroutable/not-ready/resyncing/workspace-crashed/cap-exceeded/invalid-position.

features.falsifier: a hover result and a completion result in the same response use different position bases [INV-TOOL-1]; or an oversized line/column reaches the fake LSP facade instead of being rejected before the call [INV-TOOL-5]; or a not-ready workspace is reported as an empty successful result instead of a named error [INV-TOOL-4]

features.name: java_hover tool
features.behavior: java_hover returns the resolved signature and javadoc plus a range locating the resolved token for the symbol at path/line/column, in the tool layer's 1-based coordinates; the range is never omitted on a successful result

context.note: Thin wrapper: argument shape from docs/design/tool-surface.md's tool table, result shaping (position conversion, error taxonomy, range field) delegates entirely to feat-tool-layer-core — do not re-implement conversion here.

features.falsifier: returns a hover result whose position was never converted through the tool layer's single conversion boundary, so it is silently 0-based while every other tool result is 1-based [INV-TOOL-1]; or a successful hover result omits its range field [INV-TOOL-6]

features.name: java_definition tool
features.behavior: java_definition returns the declaration location(s) for the symbol at path/line/column, in the tool layer's 1-based coordinates

context.note: Same shared shape as hover/references (docs/design/tool-surface.md#Build-order item 3) — reuse feat-tool-layer-core's validation and conversion, do not duplicate it.

features.falsifier: returns a declaration location whose line/column was never converted through the tool layer's single conversion boundary [INV-TOOL-1]

features.name: java_references tool
features.behavior: java_references returns reference locations for the symbol at path/line/column, capped and marked truncated:true with the true total when the cap is exceeded

context.note: X-008's default cap (200) is still an open cross-cutting decision — read the configured cap from the tool layer, don't hard-code a number here.

features.falsifier: a references result beyond the cap is returned uncapped instead of truncated:true plus the true total [INV-TOOL-3]

features.name: Prove: hover/definition/references answer correctly through the full boundary
features.behavior: Against a fixture containing non-ASCII and astral-plane characters, hover/definition/references all return byte-offset-correct positions (hover's carried in its always-present range), references beyond the cap are truncated with the true total, and unroutable/not-ready/oversized-coordinate/no-resolvable-element calls always produce a structured error rather than an empty success

context.note: This is the readiness probe's first real exercise (docs/design/tool-surface.md#Build-order item 3: 'they also give the readiness probe something real to assert') — run it against the real per-workspace pool, not a fake facade.

features.falsifier: a position in any of the three tools' results does not match the file's real byte offset on the non-ASCII/astral-plane fixture [INV-TOOL-1]; or a references result beyond the cap is silently truncated with no truncated:true flag [INV-TOOL-3]; or an oversized coordinate reaches the LSP call instead of being rejected first [INV-TOOL-5]; or any failure case in the sweep comes back as an empty successful result [INV-TOOL-4]; or a successful java_hover result omits its range field, or a position holding no resolvable element is reported as a successful hover result instead of INV-TOOL-4's structured no-result [INV-TOOL-6]
features.checkerNotes:
BLOCKED: navigation oracle requires callable interfaces owned by four not-started tool dependencies.

TCON-TOOL-0001 through TCON-TOOL-0010 require real java_hover, java_definition and java_references calls through the real mcp-tool-layer and per-workspace pool. docs/design/tool-surface.md specifies public arguments and observable result semantics, but no executable/CLI entry point or TypeScript/process invocation contract exists for the integration test. feat-tool-layer-core, feat-tool-hover, feat-tool-definition and feat-tool-references are all not-started. Writing the test now would invent those production interfaces or fail only on missing modules, neither of which is valid behavioral-red evidence. Implement and specify the four dependencies first, then route this proof feature back to test-implementer. The prior INV-TOOL-6 design resolution remains recorded in TP-TOOL-0001 and the approved design artifacts.

features.name: diagnostics-cache: absorb publishDiagnostics
features.behavior: The cache stores the most recent publishDiagnostics payload per URI per workspace, with a later publish for the same URI fully replacing the earlier one rather than accumulating

context.note: Diagnostics arrive unsolicited, including for files never didOpen'ed (spike B, docs/design/evidence.md) — the cache must key by URI per workspace independent of any open/close lifecycle.

features.falsifier: publishing an empty diagnostics list for a URI leaves the previously-cached problems in place instead of fully replacing them [INV-DIAG-2]

features.name: java_diagnostics tool
features.behavior: java_diagnostics returns the cached problems for a file or an entire project, distinguishing an explicit 'not reported yet' marker from an empty (clean) result

context.note: This is item 4 in the build order specifically because its shape differs from the navigation tools — it reads a push cache, it never makes its own LSP request (docs/design/tool-surface.md#Build-order).

features.falsifier: a URI with no publish yet returns the same empty list as a URI JDT LS reported zero problems for, instead of a distinct 'not reported yet' marker [INV-DIAG-1]

features.name: Prove: diagnostics are never stale, never accumulated, never cross-workspace
features.behavior: Querying before and after the first publish for a file distinguishes not-reported from clean, publishing an empty list after a real one fully clears the cache, and two workspaces sharing the same relative path never serve each other's diagnostics

context.note: Reuse the spike-B two-workspace-same-relative-path fixture shape (docs/design/evidence.md) for the cross-workspace assertion — that is the exact scenario INV-DIAG-3 exists to forbid.

features.falsifier: a query before the first publish for a URI returns the same shape as a query after a clean publish [INV-DIAG-1]; or a publish-then-empty-publish sequence leaves stale problems cached [INV-DIAG-2]; or workspace B's cache serves a diagnostic published by workspace A for the same relative path [INV-DIAG-3]
features.checkerNotes:
BLOCKED: diagnostics oracle requires callable interfaces owned by two not-started dependencies.

TCON-DIAG-0001 through TCON-DIAG-0003 require real publishDiagnostics delivery and java_diagnostics queries through distinct live workspace instances. docs/design/tool-surface.md specifies arguments and observable semantics, but it does not define an executable/CLI entry point, TypeScript signature, notification-injection contract, or concrete not-reported result shape. feat-diagnostics-cache and feat-tool-diagnostics are both not-started, so writing the integration test now would invent their production interfaces or fail only on missing modules rather than behavior. Implement and specify those dependencies first, then route this proof feature back to test-implementer.

features.name: java_completion tool
features.behavior: java_completion returns completion items for path/line/column, capped and marked truncated:true with the true total when the cap is exceeded

context.note: Build-order item 5, chosen specifically because it is the high-volume result shape that stresses the cap (docs/design/tool-surface.md#Build-order) — depends on feat-prove-diagnostics finishing first per the design's explicit sequencing, not on any data dependency.

features.falsifier: a completion result in a large scope is returned uncapped instead of truncated:true plus the true total [INV-TOOL-3]

features.name: Prove: completion never returns an uncapped or silently-cut list
